title: Why we get conned and how to avoid it, with Daniel Simons, PhD, and Christopher Chabris, PhD

sentences.en: From headline-grabbing Ponzi schemes, to email-fishing identity thieves, to fake news stories circulating on social media,
sentences.zh: 从登上头条的庞氏骗局，到通过电子邮件钓鱼的身份窃贼，再到在社交媒体上流传的虚假新闻，

sentences.en: it can sometimes seem like the world is full of people who want to deceive us.
sentences.zh: 有时看起来这个世界似乎充满了想要欺骗我们的人。

sentences.en: What many of these scammers and con artists have in common is that they take advantage of the patterns of thinking and the mental shortcuts that we all use in our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 许多骗子和诈骗犯的共同点在于，他们利用了我们在日常生活中都会使用的思维模式和心理捷径。

sentences.en: Most of the time, these mental habits serve us well.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，这些心理习惯对我们很有帮助。

sentences.en: After all, most people aren't trying to trick us and it would be difficult to go through life skeptical of everything and everyone.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，大多数人并不是想欺骗我们，如果对一切人和事都持怀疑态度，生活将很难进行。

sentences.en: But the same habits of trust and belief that work well most of the time can leave us vulnerable when we encounter a con artist, a false news story, or some other type of deceit.
sentences.zh: 但这些在大多数情况下运作良好的信任和信念习惯，当我们遇到骗子、虚假新闻或其他类型的欺骗时，却可能让我们变得脆弱。

sentences.en: So what are the cognitive habits that put us at risk of believing lies and falling prey to scams?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟是哪些认知习惯让我们面临相信谎言和落入骗局的风险呢？

sentences.en: Are some people simply more gullible than others or can anyone be conned.

sentences.en: When you're offered something that sounds like an amazing opportunity, what questions should you ask to figure out if it's too good to be true?

sentences.en: How common is fraud in the worlds of business, science, and elsewhere?

sentences.en: Is technology, including artificial intelligence, making it easier for people to cheat and lie and to get away with it?

sentences.zh: 现在，许多骗局都涉及承诺一些好得令人难以置信的事情，比如提供闻所未闻的回报的投资机会，或者一家

sentences.en: promises a miracle medical cure.
sentences.zh: 承诺奇迹般医疗治愈的公司。

sentences.en: If you're offered something that sounds like an amazing opportunity, what are the questions to ask yourself to decide if it falls into that too good to be true category?
sentences.zh: 如果有人向你提供听起来像是绝佳机会的东西，你应该问自己什么问题来判断它是否属于“好得令人难以置信”的范畴？

sentences.en: I can start with that.
sentences.zh: 我可以从这里开始说起。

sentences.en: We all know that when something is too good to be true, we shouldn't believe it, right?
sentences.zh: 我们都知道，当一件事好得令人难以置信时，我们不应该相信，对吧？

sentences.en: That's something that everybody kind of knows that if it seems too good to be true, it probably is.
sentences.zh: 这是每个人都知道的常识，如果它看起来好得令人难以置信，那它很可能就是假的。

sentences.en: The problem is what sounds too good to be true to one person is just good enough for another person.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，对一个人来说听起来好得令人难以置信的事情，对另一个人来说可能刚好合适。

sentences.en: So for somebody else, they're going to find that as just plausible enough that they're going to jump in.
sentences.zh: 所以对其他人来说，他们会觉得这足够可信，从而选择入局。

sentences.en: The challenge in deciding when something's too good to be true is in making sure that you view it kind of skeptically from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 判断一件事是否好得令人难以置信的挑战在于，要确保你从一开始就以怀疑的眼光看待它。

sentences.en: So if something seems really promising, really amazing, you should take a step back and say, what would I need to know in order to verify that that's actually true?
sentences.zh: 所以如果某件事看起来非常有前景、非常惊人，你应该退后一步问自己：为了验证它是否真实，我需要知道些什么？

sentences.en: We know that if somebody offers you 50% returns on your investment with a guarantee of no losses all within a year, almost certainly not true because no investment does that.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，如果有人向你提供50%的投资回报，并保证一年内零亏损，那几乎肯定不是真的，因为没有任何投资能做到这一点。

sentences.en: So you can take a step back and say, what would they have to be doing to be able to make that claim?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以退后一步问：他们必须怎么做才能做出这种承诺？

sentences.en: And as soon as you start questioning it a little bit, you might realize that now this really actually is too good to be true.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始产生一点怀疑，你可能就会意识到，这确实好得令人难以置信。

sentences.en: I was just going to say, what about the case of Bernie Madoff, where it was too good to be true, and yet he was paying people.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，伯纳德·麦道夫的案例又如何呢？那件事好得令人难以置信，但他确实在给人们支付回报。

sentences.en: So you didn't really have a reason to question other than, well, the market isn't behaving this well, and yet I'm still getting 15% returns every year.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的没有理由去质疑，除了“市场表现并没有这么好，但我每年却依然能拿到15%的回报”。

sentences.en: I mean, how do you escape being in a situation like that?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你如何才能避免陷入那种境地？

sentences.en: So too good to be true, as Dan said, can mean different things to different people.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如丹所说，“好得令人难以置信”对不同的人意味着不同的事情。

sentences.en: But there are some signs that are pretty common for things that are too good to be true, or at least that shouldn't be believed.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些好得令人难以置信，或者至少不应该相信的事情，有一些非常常见的迹象。

sentences.en: And in the case of Bernie Madoff, what he was offering wasn't really necessarily too good.
sentences.zh: 而在伯纳德·麦道夫的案例中，他所提供的并不一定真的“太好”。

sentences.en: It was not a really huge rate of return.
sentences.zh: 那并不是一个非常高的回报率。

sentences.en: It was 8% to 12% a year, which is a little bit above the long run average of the stock market, but not too much.
sentences.zh: 每年8%到12%，这比股市的长期平均水平略高一点，但并没有高出太多。

sentences.en: It's nothing like what an original Ponzi scheme was offering or what a lot of cryptocurrency offers recently have offered.
sentences.zh: 这与最初的庞氏骗局或最近许多加密货币提供的回报完全不同。

sentences.en: But the telltale sign was that it was every single year.
sentences.zh: 但最明显的迹象是，它每年都是如此。

sentences.en: There was never a losing year
sentences.zh: 从来没有亏损的一年。

sentences.en: There was barely ever even a losing month.
sentences.zh: 甚至几乎没有亏损的一个月。

sentences.en: He managed to make the returns on his investors' investments fit within that narrow band.
sentences.zh: 他设法让投资者的投资回报保持在那个狭窄的区间内。

sentences.en: So the excessive consistency there was, I think, what trapped people.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，那种过度的稳定性才是困住人们的原因。

sentences.en: They thought, this is a sure thing.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，这是一笔稳赚不赔的买卖。

sentences.en: I will never lose.
sentences.zh: 我永远不会亏损。

sentences.en: I'll get the same amount per year, kind of like a treasury bill or some kind of bond or savings account, but just with a much higher rate of return.
sentences.zh: 我每年都能拿到同样的金额，就像国库券、某种债券或储蓄账户一样，只是回报率高得多。

sentences.en: And that was, I think, the innovation, like really the true novelty of Madoff's.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是创新，也就是麦道夫真正的独特之处。

sentences.en: It's called a Ponzi scheme, but some people call it a Madoff scheme because he really
sentences.zh: 它被称为庞氏骗局，但有些人称之为麦道夫骗局，因为他确实

sentences.en: added this new dimension of not offering people the ridiculous proposition that educated people
sentences.zh: 增加了一个新的维度，即不再向人们提供那种受过教育的人

sentences.en: maybe who've been in the stock market for a while know is unrealistic, the 50% in six months or a year or something like that.
sentences.zh: ——可能在股市摸爬滚打了一段时间的人——都知道是不现实的荒谬提议，比如半年或一年内获得50%的回报之类的。

sentences.en: But offering something that seems much more reasonable, it wasn't too good to be true in the sense of the total amount of money they made, it was too good to be true in the sense
sentences.zh: 而是提供了一些看起来更合理的东西，从他们赚取的总金额来看，它并不算“好得令人难以置信”，但从

sentences.en: of the consistency with which they made it.
sentences.zh: 他们赚取回报的稳定性来看，它确实好得令人难以置信。

sentences.en: So consistency or the lack of it is an important sort of sign of fraud that people can pay more attention to than they might otherwise.
sentences.zh: 所以，稳定性或其缺乏，是一种重要的欺诈迹象，人们可以比以往更加关注这一点。

sentences.en: That happens in science too, right?
sentences.zh: 这种情况在科学界也存在，对吧？

sentences.en: So one of the hallmarks of fraud in clinical trials is if the baseline conditions, when people are measured at the beginning, you'll often do checks to make
sentences.zh: 临床试验中欺诈的标志之一是，如果基线条件——即人们在开始时被测量的数据——你通常会进行检查以

sentences.en: sure that the people assigned to the treatment and the placebo group were the same in other ways so that those aren't sort of contaminating the effects of your treatment.
sentences.zh: 确保分配到治疗组和安慰剂组的人在其他方面是相同的，这样这些因素就不会污染你治疗效果的评估。

sentences.en: So you kind of expect the two groups to be balanced on prior health conditions, for example, or age.
sentences.zh: 所以你通常期望两组在既往健康状况或年龄等方面是平衡的。

sentences.en: And if they're all perfectly balanced, that's weird.
sentences.zh: 如果它们完全平衡，那就很奇怪了。

sentences.en: That's a red flag because just by chance, if you randomly assign people to groups, they won't all end up perfectly balanced.
sentences.zh: 这是一个危险信号，因为如果你随机分配人员，他们不可能最终完全平衡。

sentences.en: You'll end up with a distribution with some differing on some factors and not on others.
sentences.zh: 你最终会得到一个分布，其中一些人在某些因素上有所不同，而在另一些因素上则相同。

sentences.en: And it's turned out that that's been a major way of finding fraud in a number of disciplines from anesthesiology to any field that has clinical medical trials.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这已成为从麻醉学到任何有临床医学试验的领域中，发现欺诈行为的主要方法。

sentences.en: So your book warns people to be wary of the butterfly effect.
sentences.zh: 所以你的书警告人们要警惕蝴蝶效应。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, so the old anecdote goes that a butterfly flapping its wings in Brazil can cause a tornado in Texas.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有句老话是说，在巴西拍动翅膀的蝴蝶可能会在德克萨斯州引发龙卷风。

sentences.en: And that's based on sort of old, well, not old, but relatively new ideas about chaos theory and certain attempts to model how small changes in
sentences.zh: 这基于某种古老的——好吧，不算古老，但相对较新的混沌理论思想，以及某些试图模拟微小变化如何

sentences.en: one place can perturb a system so that some dramatic thing happens someplace else.
sentences.zh: 在一个地方扰动系统，从而在另一个地方引发某种戏剧性事件的尝试。

sentences.en: People tend to be too accepting of the idea that tiny little interventions in the world, not random
sentences.zh: 人们往往太容易接受这种观点，即世界上微小的干预措施——不是像蝴蝶拍动翅膀那样随机的

sentences.en: things like butterflies flapping their wings, but maybe very small, very small, very brief interventions.
sentences.zh: 事情，而是可能非常微小、非常短暂的干预。

sentences.en: For example, giving like a half hour or an hour long sort of like reflective exercise at the beginning of college can cause big changes in people's GPA and willingness to
sentences.zh: 例如，在大学开学时进行半小时或一小时的反思练习，就能对人们的平均绩点（GPA）以及是否愿意

sentences.en: stay in college and complete the degree and so on.
sentences.zh: 留在大学并完成学位等方面产生重大影响。

sentences.en: Just to give one example of this class of this class of effects.
sentences.zh: 这只是这类效应的一个例子。

sentences.en: Another one is priming studies, the idea that sort of very brief exposures to stimuli we don't notice or remember encountering can dramatically change our
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是启动效应研究，即认为我们没有注意到或不记得接触过的刺激，哪怕只是非常短暂的接触，也能戏剧性地改变我们的

sentences.en: behaviors or beliefs, you know, just a few seconds, minutes, or even longer later.
sentences.zh: 行为或信念，你知道，就在几秒钟、几分钟甚至更久之后。

sentences.en: There's one particular dramatic example where a study claimed that subliminally seeing the Israeli flag
sentences.zh: 有一个特别戏剧性的例子，一项研究声称潜意识地看到以色列国旗

sentences.en: caused people to be more likely to vote and vote for centrist parties as opposed to more extreme parties, you know, days, weeks later in an actual election.
sentences.zh: 会导致人们在实际选举中更有可能投票，并且更有可能投票给中间派政党，而不是更极端的政党，你知道，这可是几天、几周之后的事。

sentences.en: And that's just the kind of thing that you should look up and say, how plausible is it that something that happened to you for 150
sentences.zh: 这正是你应该去查证并思考的事情：一个人在10月份经历了150毫秒的刺激，

sentences.en: milliseconds, you know, in October changed, you know, what you did in the voting booth in November.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这改变了你在11月份投票站的行为，这种可能性有多大？

sentences.en: And there are many, many studies and stories like this, which we sort of take to mean that there's an inherent appeal to the idea that we could discover these little tiny things
sentences.zh: 有许多许多这样的研究和故事，我们将其理解为：人们天生倾向于相信我们能发现这些微不足道的小事，

sentences.en: that made a vast difference.
sentences.zh: 并能带来巨大的差异。

sentences.en: And if we did discover them, that would be great, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的发现了它们，那不是很好吗？

sentences.en: It's not irrational to say we should want tiny, cheap things that make huge outcomes.
sentences.zh: 说我们应该追求那些能带来巨大成果的微小、廉价的事物，这并不非理性。

sentences.en: A vaccine is one of those things, right?
sentences.zh: 疫苗就是其中之一，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a tiny little injection that you get once that might prevent you from getting a disease for the rest of your life in some cases.
sentences.zh: 这是一种你只需接种一次的微小注射，在某些情况下，它可能让你终身免受某种疾病的困扰。

sentences.en: It's just that those are rare.
sentences.zh: 只是这种情况很少见。

sentences.en: Those are rare events in science.
sentences.zh: 这些在科学界属于罕见事件。

sentences.en: They're not the things that are coming out every day in our psychology journals, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，它们并不是每天出现在心理学期刊上的那种东西。

sentences.en: And that's a sort of general principle that anytime you see a big effect from a small intervention, that's when you should require the strongest evidence.
sentences.zh: 这是一个普遍原则：每当你看到微小的干预产生巨大的效果时，你就应该要求最强有力的证据。

sentences.en: You shouldn't go to the bank on a single study showing something like that because the odds are good in those sorts of cases that it's not going to replicate in the same way that we think we are,
sentences.zh: 你不应该仅仅因为一项研究显示了这样的结果就全盘相信，因为在这种情况下，它很可能无法像我们预想的那样复现，

sentences.en: or it's not going to be general in the way that it was claimed.
sentences.zh: 或者它不会像所声称的那样具有普遍性。

sentences.en: those are going to be the effects that are sort of really engaging and exciting and more likely to
sentences.zh: 那些往往是看起来非常吸引人、令人兴奋的效果，但更有可能

sentences.en: be wrong because it's really rare to have giant effect sizes from tiny little variation, tiny little interventions.
sentences.zh: 是错误的，因为从微小的变化、微小的干预中获得巨大的效应是非常罕见的。

sentences.en: So, do either of you have a favorite con or scam you came across in researching the book?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们在研究这本书的过程中，有没有遇到过最喜欢的骗局？

sentences.en: And I'm using the word favorite in air quotes here.
sentences.zh: 我这里的“最喜欢”是加了引号的。

sentences.en: And why is it your favorite and what can we learn from it?
sentences.zh: 为什么它是你最喜欢的，我们能从中吸取什么教训？

sentences.en: I'll start with one that I knew about before we started writing the book, but I learned a lot more about it in researching the book.
sentences.zh: 我先说一个我在写书之前就知道的，但在研究过程中我又了解了很多细节的案例。

sentences.en: And that's the famous case of John von Neumann.
sentences.zh: 那就是著名的约翰·冯·诺依曼（John von Neumann）案例。

sentences.en: And you may have heard of John von Neumann as a famous economist, mathematician, computer scientist, game theorist, one of really the fathers of sort of modern science.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过约翰·冯·诺依曼，他是一位著名的经济学家、数学家、计算机科学家、博弈论专家，确实是现代科学之父之一。

sentences.en: But it was also the name taken by a guy who entered a chess tournament in 1993 under that name.
sentences.zh: 但这也是一个在1993年以这个名字参加国际象棋比赛的人所用的名字。

sentences.en: I don't think it was his real name, but he entered a chess tournament under that name.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那是他的真名，但他确实用了这个名字参加了比赛。

sentences.en: In 1993, this was 30 years ago, actually 30 years ago this month, in fact,
sentences.zh: 那是1993年，也就是30年前，事实上正好是30年前的这个月，

sentences.en: July 1993.
And nobody had ever heard of the guy before.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，没人听说过这个人。

sentences.en: He didn't even play chess.
sentences.zh: 他甚至根本不会下棋。

sentences.en: He didn't even touch the pieces and move the pieces as though he had ever played in a chess tournament before.
sentences.zh: 他甚至连碰棋子和移动棋子的样子，都不像是一个以前参加过国际象棋比赛的人。

sentences.en: He looked like a complete outsider and novice.
sentences.zh: 他看起来完全是个外行和新手。

sentences.en: And yet he drew with a grandmaster and beat masters and was doing really well in this chess tournament.
sentences.zh: 然而，他却与一位特级大师打平，击败了大师级选手，在这场比赛中表现得非常好。

sentences.en: And in fact, tied for a prize at the end.
sentences.zh: 事实上，最后还并列获得了奖项。

sentences.en: He didn't win every game.
sentences.zh: 他并不是每局都赢。

sentences.en: Some games he would just sort of like suddenly like stop playing for no reason for 40 minutes and just let his time run out.
sentences.zh: 有些比赛他会突然无缘无故地停止下棋，长达40分钟，任由时间耗尽。

sentences.en: Or some games he would try to make illegal moves and just, you know, sort of stop.
sentences.zh: 或者有些比赛他会尝试走违规的棋，然后，你知道，就停下来。

sentences.en: At the end of the tournament, though, he had won enough games to win a prize, but everybody was suspicious about how this guy could be doing it.
sentences.zh: 不过在比赛结束时，他赢的局数足以让他获奖，但每个人都怀疑这家伙是怎么做到的。

sentences.en: And so they didn't really know exactly how, but they thought he couldn't, like this can't happen.
sentences.zh: 他们并不确切知道是怎么回事，但他们认为他不可能做到，这根本不可能发生。

sentences.en: So the tournament director, a guy named Bill Goitschberg, who I've actually known since the very first chess tournament I played in,
sentences.zh: 所以比赛主管，一个叫比尔·戈伊奇伯格（Bill Goitschberg）的人——我从我参加的第一场国际象棋比赛起就认识他了——

sentences.en: didn't want to give money to this guy who he thought might be cheating somehow.
sentences.zh: 不想给这个他认为可能以某种方式作弊的人发奖金。

sentences.en: But he didn't know whether he was cheating or how he was cheating.
sentences.zh: 但他不知道他是否在作弊，也不知道他是如何作弊的。

sentences.en: So he set up on the chessboard, before writing him a check,
sentences.zh: 所以在给他开支票之前，他在棋盘上摆了一个

sentences.en: he set up on the chessboard a very simple chess puzzle that a five-year-old who had learned the game a month earlier could probably have solved.
sentences.zh: 非常简单的残局，一个一个月前刚学会下棋的五岁小孩可能都能解开。

sentences.en: and he refused to even try it.
sentences.zh: 但他甚至拒绝尝试。

sentences.en: And he walked out and essentially was never seen before.
sentences.zh: 他直接走了出去，基本上从此销声匿迹了。

sentences.en: And so the reason why I love that con so much, um, and it's generally agreed now that basically what
sentences.zh: 我之所以那么喜欢这个骗局，嗯，现在大家普遍认为，基本上

sentences.en: the guy was doing was probably concealing an earpiece and getting information transmitted to
sentences.zh: 那家伙当时可能藏了一个耳机，并从同伙那里接收信息，

sentences.en: him by an accomplice who was using a computer to help figure out what moves to play and was sort
sentences.zh: 同伙利用计算机帮助计算出该走哪步棋，并以某种方式

sentences.en: of sending code to him, like through an earpiece saying, you know, move this piece from here to there.
sentences.zh: 通过耳机向他发送指令，比如，你知道，把这枚棋子从这里移到那里。

sentences.en: But if the transmission broke down, he would just stop and wait to hear something, you you know, and so that didn't help him solve the puzzle at the end, you know.
sentences.zh: 但如果传输中断，他就会停下来等待接收信息，你知道，所以这对他最后解那个残局没用，你知道。

sentences.en: So what the lesson that we drew from this for what you can do yourself is, you know, it would be tempting to
sentences.zh: 所以我们从中得出的教训是，你可以自己做点什么，你知道，直接开支票然后了事是很诱人的，

sentences.en: just write the check and move on, you know, and our habit of efficiency sort of leads us to sort of just, you know, move on with things like make quick decisions and so on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们追求效率的习惯往往导致我们只是，你知道，草草了事，比如快速做出决定等等。

sentences.en: But Goitschberg thought to ask one more question of this guy and do a little tiny test and see whether he really was what he purported to be that as a chess master.
sentences.zh: 但戈伊奇伯格想到了再问那家伙一个问题，做一个小小的测试，看看他是否真的是他所声称的那种国际象棋大师。
